title: Building an Equation from Slope and One Point

scenes.title: Slope + one point?
body: Write the equation of a line with slope 3 through (2, 5).
Understand what the numbers mean first.
scenes.narration: Suppose you are asked to write the equation of a line with slope three that passes through the point two, five. Before using a formula, understand what those two pieces of information mean.

scenes.title: What slope 3 means
scenes.narration: Slope tells us the line's rate of change. A slope of three means three over one: every time x moves one unit to the right, y moves three units up.

scenes.title: Use the known point
body: The line must pass through x = 2, y = 5
scenes.narration: The point two, five tells us exactly where the line passes. When x equals two, y must equal five. Now we know the direction of the line and one exact location on it.

scenes.title: Point-slope form
scenes.narration: Use point-slope form: y minus y one equals m times x minus x one. Substitute m equals three, x one equals two, and y one equals five. That gives y minus five equals three times x minus two.

scenes.title: Solve and check
scenes.narration: Distribute the three: y minus five equals three x minus six. Add five to both sides, so y equals three x minus one. Check the point: three times two minus one equals five, so the equation is correct. The full lesson is available on SUMMIT. Find the complete lesson below.
